---
title: "Reading pairs plots of posterior draws"
execute:
  enabled: true
  echo: true
  warning: false
  message: false
---

A trace plot shows one parameter across iterations. A **pairs plot** shows joint draws and can reveal dependence or locate a computational warning in parameter space. The plot must distinguish inference from a diagnostic manipulation.

## Production PCT geometry

```{r}
#| label: load-provo-pair-draws
library(ggplot2)
library(posterior)

provo <- read.csv("data/provo/passage-summaries.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cache <- readRDS(
  "data/provo/provo-stan-draw-cache.rds"
)
production <- as.data.frame(as_draws_df(subset_draws(
  cache$production_draws, variable = c("mu", "sigma")
)))
stress <- as.data.frame(as_draws_df(subset_draws(
  cache$stress_draws, variable = c("mu", "sigma")
)))
stress_diagnostics <- as.data.frame(as_draws_df(cache$stress_diagnostics))
stress$divergent <- as.logical(stress_diagnostics$divergent__)

production_correlation <- cor(production$mu, production$sigma)
stress_correlation <- cor(stress$mu, stress$sigma)
stopifnot(nrow(provo) == 55L, nrow(production) == 4000L,
          nrow(stress) == 1000L, sum(stress$divergent) > 0L)
data.frame(fit = c("production", "coarse unadapted stress"),
           correlation = c(production_correlation, stress_correlation))
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-provo-production-pairs
#| fig-cap: "Joint mu and sigma draws from the production adapted-NUTS fit."
production_opacity <- .18
ggplot(production, aes(mu, sigma)) +
  geom_point(color = "grey35", alpha = production_opacity, size = .65) +
  labs(x = "Passage-level contrast (mu)",
       y = "Passage contrast scale (sigma)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

A roughly circular cloud suggests weak linear dependence for this parameter pair, while a diagonal ellipse suggests that combinations along one direction remain plausible. Curvature or changing width may be more difficult for a constant mass matrix. Shape alone does not identify its cause.

## Locating the stress warning

```{r}
#| label: plot-provo-stress-pairs
#| fig-cap: "Joint draws from the coarse, unadapted stress computation. Divergent transitions are marked in the accent color; this is not the production posterior display."
stress_opacity <- .35
divergent_opacity <- .75
ggplot(stress, aes(mu, sigma)) +
  geom_point(color = "grey68", alpha = stress_opacity, size = .75) +
  geom_point(data = subset(stress, divergent),
             color = "#8B1A1A", alpha = divergent_opacity, size = 1.1) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-.015, .035), ylim = c(.025, .070)) +
  labs(x = "Passage-level contrast (mu)",
       y = "Passage contrast scale (sigma)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

Marked transitions locate where the intentionally degraded integrator failed. They do not constitute posterior evidence about $\mu$ or $\sigma$, and they should not be combined with production draws.

A matrix of every parameter pair quickly becomes unreadable. Select pairs implicated by the model structure or another diagnostic. A compact cloud establishes neither causal relations among parameters nor model fit; both claims require additional assumptions or checks.

## Check your understanding

1. What does a diagonal posterior cloud show directly?
2. What can a divergence overlay locate?
3. Why are the production and stress displays separated?
4. Why does a compact pairs plot not establish model adequacy?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. A diagonal posterior cloud shows linear posterior association: plausible parameter combinations lie along a common direction. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. A divergence overlay locates the part of joint parameter space where numerical integration failed. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. The production draws represent inference, while the coarse stress draws are a deliberately degraded diagnostic manipulation and must not be pooled with them. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. A compact pairs plot shows only selected joint parameter geometry; it does not compare replicated linguistic data with observations. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>
